titulo.en: From the district to the State

intro.en: How a country is divided, who represents it, and words for war, crime and belief that appear in every newspaper.

el Tercer Mundo.nota: Historical expression; avoid using it as a neutral label for countries today.

texto.en:
**Territory.** Spain is divided into seventeen **comunidades autónomas** and fifty **provincias**. A big city is divided into **distritos** and **barrios**. **La nación**, **el Estado**, **el país**.

**Institutions.** **El Congreso** and **el Senado** form **el parlamento**. The government has **un presidente**, **vicepresidentes** and **ministros**: **de Interior**, **de Defensa**, **de Educación**, **de Asuntos Exteriores**. Abroad, a country has **una embajada** in the capital, with **un embajador**, and **consulados** in other cities, each with **un cónsul**. Beyond the country: **la Unión Europea (UE)** and **la ONU**.

**If you lose your passport** abroad, you go to **el consulado**.

**The army.** **Un soldado**, **un capitán**, **un general**: all are **militares**. **Una guerra civil**, **mundial**, **de independencia**. **Estar en guerra.** **Una pistola**, **una bomba**.

**Crime.** **Un ladrón** roba; **un asesino** mata; **un terrorista** commits **un atentado**. Something against the law **es ilegal**, and the guilty **van a la cárcel**.

**The world.** **Los países de ingresos altos / bajos**, **los países en desarrollo**, **la desigualdad** and **el progreso**. **Tercer Mundo** is a historical expression; avoid using it as a neutral label for countries today.

**Manners.** **La cortesía**, **la amabilidad**; **ser amable**, **ser buena persona**.

**Belief.** **Cristiano**, **católico**, **protestante**, **musulmán**, **judío**. **El sacerdote** says mass. **La Biblia**, **el Corán**. **El cielo** and **el infierno**.

frases.es: El último día de mi viaje a Marruecos perdí el pasaporte, o quizá me lo robó un ladrón muy hábil.
frases.en: On the last day of my trip to Morocco I lost my passport, or perhaps a very skilful thief stole it from me.
analisis: El último día de mi viaje a Marruecos

frases.es: En la comisaría, un policía me explicó con mucha amabilidad que tenía que ir al consulado.
frases.en: At the police station, an officer explained to me very kindly that I had to go to the consulate.

frases.es: La embajada estaba en la capital, a trescientos kilómetros, pero había un consulado en mi misma ciudad.
frases.en: The embassy was in the capital, three hundred kilometres away, but there was a consulate in the very city I was in.

frases.es: Delante de la puerta había dos soldados, y dentro, una cola de personas con el mismo problema.
frases.en: In front of the door there were two soldiers, and inside, a queue of people with the same problem.

frases.es: El cónsul firmó un documento provisional para que pudiera volver a España.
frases.en: The consul signed a temporary document so that I could return to Spain.

frases.es: Me dijo que debía comprobar qué documentos necesitaba para volver a España, y me deseó buen viaje.
frases.en: He told me I should check which documents I needed to return to Spain, and wished me a good journey.

pregunta.en: According to the text, where did the traveller get a new document?

At the consulate.en: El cónsul firmó un documento provisional.

At the embassy.en: It was three hundred kilometres away.

At the police station.en: They sent him to the consulate.

texto.en: They dealt with me very kindly.
They attended me with many friends.
They waited for me with much love.

explicacion.en: Atender: to deal with. Amabilidad: kindness.

bloques.frase: Tuve que ir al consulado para pedir otro pasaporte

traduccion.en: I had to go to the consulate to ask for another passport.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Explain how your country is divided and governed, from the town to the State.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Tell aloud what you would do if you lost your passport abroad.
